_readme: The retention checks — what the edit measures on every run so the machine is dialled for attention and acquisition (the owner, 2026-09-23: 'we are literally programming ads for social media'). machine/retention.py reads these rows; every number is a DIAL the owner can change here (or per run in controls.json → retention.dials). NOTHING here blocks an export (the owner, 2026-09-23: 'don't worry about the feed ads run 6–15 seconds or hooks lands in the first 3 seconds'): the two evidence-backed rules are INFO lines in the report, every other rule is a WARN with a score. `evidence: evidence` = a platform study stands behind the number; `house-style` = common editor practice, no study found — our own number, tune it. Source for both: the social-edit-libraries research, 2026-09-23.

placement.what: where this piece runs — only the length line in the report reads it; it never blocks

organic.name: Organic TikTok / Reels
organic.note: no length band — organic has no fixed sweet spot

meta-feed.name: Meta Feed ad
meta-feed.note: Meta's own Feed guidance: 6–15 s when the format allows

rules.name: Hook lands in the first 3 s
rules.rule: Hook text is on screen from frame one AND the hook line is spoken (or the hook text stays up long enough to read) by 3.0 s.
rules.source: Facebook IQ via leadsbridge.com/blog/meta-ads-best-practices — 65% who reach 3 s go on to 10 s; 23% more brand recall when the brand is in the first 3 s
rules.note: Info only, never a gate (the owner, 2026-09-23).

rules.name: Length fits the placement
rules.rule: The piece runs inside the placement's length band (placement dial above). Organic has no band.
rules.note: Info only, never a gate (the owner, 2026-09-23).

rules.name: No static hold
rules.rule: Something changes at least every N seconds: a cut, a zoom/punch-in, a new caption line, a sound effect or a graphic. A longer stretch is flagged at its seconds.
rules.source: MrBeast-style retention editing, observed practice (air.io retention-editing guide) — no study behind the number

rules.name: Visual change cadence
rules.rule: At least one VISUAL change (cut, zoom, graphic, transition) every N seconds — captions and sound do not count here.
rules.source: 'pattern interrupt every 3–5 s' — repeated across editor guides, no study cited (joyspace.ai)

rules.name: No dead air left in
rules.rule: No silence longer than N seconds between words while someone is on screen talking or the voice is running. Silent plates (cards, splits, end card) are silent on purpose and are not counted.
rules.source: top retention editors cut every pause (air.io) — practice, not measured

rules.name: Caption pops carry a sound
rules.rule: Share of caption pops (each new caption line) with a sound effect landing within the window of it.
rules.source: 'every word-pop gets an SFX hit' — editor practice; house style says every pop, the dial starts at half

rules.name: Zoom on the emphasis words
rules.rule: Share of emphasis words with a zoom (a punch-in cut, a zoom transition, a zoom move) within the window of the word. Emphasis = words marked `emphasis` on the sheet, else the loudest share of words in the rendered sound, else numbers / ALL CAPS / '!' words.
rules.source: 'something changes every second, zoom on the stressed word' — editor practice, no number found

rules.name: Cutaways in talking runs
rules.rule: In a talking run (the presenter on screen with nothing laid over), a B-roll, insert or graphic at least every N seconds.
rules.source: B-roll cadence — editor practice, no numeric source found; our own threshold

rules.name: Words on screen within 1 s
rules.rule: Some text (the hook, a caption, a card) is on screen by N seconds.
rules.source: partly backed by the 3-second / brand-recall data (Facebook IQ); the 1 s figure itself is house style

rules.name: Loop-friendly ending
rules.rule: How much the last frame looks like the first (SSIM 0–1, measured by ffmpeg on the rendered file). A score, not a must.
rules.source: loop endings — common editor practice, no study found; an optional style flag

beats.what: machine/beats.py: B-roll hand-offs and graphic hits move to the nearest music beat when one is this close; talking cuts never move (the lips)
